headline: The biggest winner from Spirit's collapse: the stock doubled, now trades above its consensus target, and 42% of the float is short.
business: Frontier is now the largest U.S. ultra-low-cost carrier, with an all-Airbus A320neo-family fleet and the industry's lowest unit costs. It earns heavily from ancillary fees and absorbed displaced Spirit demand after Spirit shut down in May 2026.
recent: Q3 2026 revenue of $1.36B (+53%, the fastest growth in the industry); fare revenue per passenger +71% to $67.82; passengers +18%.
Adjusted profit of $40M beat expectations; GAAP net loss of $104M on lease termination and fleet charges. Fuel expense +82%.
Q4 guided to adjusted EPS of -$0.15 to +$0.05 at $4.75/gal fuel, with RASM up more than 20% and capacity +5-6%.
strengths: Lowest cost base in the industry
risks: Negative TTM EBITDA and operating margin (-9.5%)
Labor and fuel inflation hit thin ULCC margins hardest
catalysts: Q4 results and 2027 guidance: first full year without Spirit
